judged_text: The Zoho-Bigin refresh call passes `credentialId` as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens, while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, zohocrm, lark, zoom, webex, o365) passes `credential.userId` — a confusable-pair binding where the credential row id is sent as calcomUserId. In sync mode the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT receives the credential's database id in the `calcomUserId` field, so the parent application resolves the wrong user (or none) and returns/updates credentials for the wrong account, silently corrupting or failing Zoho-Bigin token sync.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The Zoho-Bigin refresh call passes `credentialId` as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens, while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, zohocrm, lark, zoom, webex, o365) passes `credential.userId` — a confusable-pair binding where the credential row id is sent as calcomUserId. In sync mode the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT receives the credential's database id in the `calcomUserId` field, so the parent application resolves the wrong user (or none) and returns/updates credentials for the wrong account, silently corrupting or failing Zoho-Bigin token sync.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` into the `userId` parameter (per `refreshOAuthTokens` signature: `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)`). All other updated call sites pass `credential.userId`. In sync mode, `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so using a credential identifier variable instead of the user’s id would cause the sync endpoint to look up the wrong user or none.
